deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A is a compact operator on a Hilbert space H. Write s_p(A) = Σ|λ_i(A)|^p for the eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, and S_p(A) = Σ μ_i(A)^p = ||A||_p^p for the singular values μ_i = λ_i(|A|). The goal is formula (5) of the notes, Weyl's inequality s_p(A) ≤ S_p(A) for all 0 < p < ∞. Grothendieck remarks on the previous page that he knows only a 'complicated' proof of it. The proof proceeds in four steps.

Step 1 (0 < p < 1, entire functions). Take A trace class and f(z) = det(1 - zA), an entire function of order ≤ 1 with f(0) = 1, whose zeros are the 1/λ_i. Let n(t) count the zeros and N(r) = ∫_0^r n(t)/t dt. Jensen gives N(r) ≤ log M(r). Integrating by parts twice:
 Σ|a_i|^{-p} = p ∫ n(t) t^{-p-1} dt = p^2 ∫ N(t) t^{-p-1} dt ≤ p^2 ∫_0^∞ log M_A(r) r^{-p-1} dr.
This is the 'classical bound' he invokes.

Step 2 (comparison of maximum moduli). He uses M_A(r) ≤ M_{|A|}(r) = det(1 + r|A|); the justification is left blank '(......)'. Then formula (9) applies, with ∫_0^∞ log(1+rs) r^{-1-p} dr = s^p π/(p sin πp). This yields
 (10) s_p(A) ≤ (pπ / sin pπ) S_p(A).
The constant k(p) = pπ/sin pπ is > 1 and tends to 1 as p → 0.

Step 3 (power trick). For arbitrary p, pick n with p/n < 1. Eigenvalues of A^n are λ_i^n (Riesz theory), so s_p(A) = s_{p/n}(A^n). Hence s_p(A) ≤ k(p/n) S_{p/n}(A^n).

Step 4 (Hölder). The generalized Hölder inequality (6) for Schatten quasi-norms gives ||A^n||_{p/n} ≤ ||A||_p^n. Therefore S_{p/n}(A^n) ≤ S_p(A), and so s_p(A) ≤ k(p/n) S_p(A). The next page writes this with r/p in place of p/n and lets the integer tend to ∞. Since k(p/n) → 1, this gives s_p(A) ≤ S_p(A), which is Weyl's inequality.

Purpose. These are lemmas on Schatten classes L^p for 0 < p < ∞: quasi-triangle inequality (4), Weyl (5), Hölder (6). They are background for Grothendieck's 1953–55 work on Fredholm theory and eigenvalue distribution of nuclear and p-summing operators (Produits tensoriels topologiques; La théorie de Fredholm).
errors: The step M_A(r) ≤ M_{|A|}(r), i.e. |det(1+zA)| ≤ det(1+|z||A|), is left unjustified ('(......)'). It is true: in finite dimension s_i(1+X) ≤ 1 + s_i(X) by Weyl/Ky Fan, then approximate. But it is a genuine gap on the page.

He calls Hölder (6) for products, including exponents < 1, 'élémentaire'. For quasi-norms with p < 1 it really rests on Horn's inequality Π_{j≤k} s_j(AB) ≤ Π_{j≤k} s_j(A)s_j(B) plus a majorization argument. His own attempt at (6) on the next page, via formula (9), is crossed out. So the 'elementary' claim is optimistic, though the argument is not circular.
Label clash: '(10)' is used both for M_{|A+B|} ≤ M_{|A|}M_{|B|} on the previous page and for s_p ≤ (pπ/sin pπ) S_p here.
Step 1 needs A trace class (f of order ≤ 1, boundary terms vanishing for p < 1). The general case needs the remark that s_p and S_p finite reduce to this, or an approximation; this is implicit.
The next page mixes the letters r, p and n when stating the final inequality; this is notational only.

ideas.what: Bounding Σ|λ_i|^p via the Jensen/Lindelöf integral p^2∫ log M(r) r^{-p-1} dr applied to the Fredholm determinant det(1 - zA)
ideas.modern_name: Entire-function (Fredholm determinant) approach to eigenvalue estimates; Carleman-type inequalities
ideas.usually_credited_to: Carleman (1921), Hille–Tamarkin, Lalesco; later Gohberg–Krein, Simon (Trace Ideals)
ideas.where_published: Same flavour in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) and Produits tensoriels topologiques ch. II (eigenvalue/order estimates of Fredholm determinants)

ideas.what: Explicit integral formula S_p(A) = (p sin πp/π) ∫_0^∞ log det(1+r|A|) r^{-1-p} dr, giving the constant pπ/sin pπ in s_p ≤ k(p) S_p for p < 1
ideas.modern_name: Mellin-type representation of Schatten quasi-norms via Fredholm determinants

ideas.what: Power/amplification trick: s_p(A) = s_{p/n}(A^n), together with S_{p/n}(A^n) ≤ S_p(A), removes a constant k(p/n) → 1
ideas.modern_name: Power trick / tensor-power-style amplification in eigenvalue distribution theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Widely used by Pietsch, König, Johnson–König–Maurey–Retherford (1970s–80s); classical antecedents in Weyl/Horn-type arguments

ideas.what: Weyl's inequality Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ Σ s_i^p for all p > 0
ideas.where_published: Used and cited in Produits tensoriels topologiques / Fredholm theory papers

ideas.what: Hölder inequality for Schatten quasi-norms, iterated: ||A^n||_{p/n} ≤ ||A||_p^n
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for Schatten classes (all p > 0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Horn (1950), Ky Fan, von Neumann/Schatten for p ≥ 1

missed.claim: Grothendieck gives a proof of Weyl's inequality that avoids majorization theory. It uses only the Jensen-type bound on zeros of the Fredholm determinant, the elementary determinant comparison, Hölder, and a power trick with the explicit constant pπ/sin pπ → 1. This anticipates the 'power trick plus entire functions' style later systematized in Pietsch/König eigenvalue distribution theory. It is a nice early instance, but the result itself is classical.
missed.quote: Le facteur pπ/sin pπ est >1, mais tend vers 1 pour p→0. ... On a évidemment s_p(A) = s_{p/n}(A^n)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck using the amplification/power trick for eigenvalue inequalities in 1953, before its popularization in Banach-space eigenvalue theory. It is of no new mathematical content.

deep.surprise_reason: The result (Weyl's inequality) is classical (1949). The proof route — Fredholm determinant growth, power trick with constant tending to 1 — is elegant and an early example of a technique later central in eigenvalue distribution theory, but it is not a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: In 'f(z) = det(1 - zA)' the sign is obscured by an ink blot in the image ('1 ▬ z A'); it may be '+'. Either sign works for the argument.
The justification after 'M_A(r) ≤ M_{|A|}(r)' is a blank '( ...... )' in the manuscript, not illegible text.
The leading crossed-out word before 's_p(A) ≤ p^2∫...' is a struck-out abbreviation (perhaps 'Cor'), not mathematical content.
'Or, on a' is preceded by a crossed-out 'S_{p/n}(A^n) ≤ S_p(A)', correctly marked as deleted.
